finding: The prior verifier and exact-run binder left discovery, JWKS retrieval, GitHub token endpoint confinement, token disposal, and receipt production as separate workflow responsibilities. A composed fail-closed pipeline can enforce those transitions without retaining or emitting the bearer token.

observed_claims: GitHub Actions jobs can request unique short-lived OIDC JWTs.
The documented JOSE algorithm is RS256.
Documented claims include repository, repository_id, run_id, run_attempt, runner_environment, issuer, iat, nbf, and exp.
GitHub exposes an OIDC discovery document from the canonical token.actions.githubusercontent.com issuer.

verification.method: node --test with mocked discovery, JWKS, token endpoint, generated RSA keypair, signed JWT, and exact-run expectations
verification.execution_environment: ephemeral local test harness using repository-compatible Node CommonJS modules

uncertainty: No live GitHub Actions OIDC token was requested.
No network-failure retry policy or JWKS cache policy is implemented.

The pipeline does not establish same-process execution, trusted runner integrity, hardware attestation, transcript truth, deployment identity, browser behavior, audio audibility, or physical-device behavior.
falsification_route: Show that a non-HTTPS or non-GitHub request/JWKS host is accepted.
Show that an issuer-substituted discovery document is accepted.
Show that an invalid RS256 signature or wrong audience is accepted.
Show that exact repository, workflow SHA, run ID, attempt, or transcript digest mismatches are accepted.
Show that the returned object contains the raw bearer token.
